title: Clearing Hold on Check and Bank-Transfer Grace-Cure Payments — Premium Billing Accounts
content:
**Rule.** On Premium Billing Accounts, a grace-cure payment by check or by bank transfer (EFT) is held until it clears, and a held payment does not count: its amount is added back to the grace-cure payment now being taken. The amount added back joins the other additions to the past-due premium; the total, after any deduction, is floored at 0.00 and rounded half up to the cent once, at the end.

**Length of the hold**
| Returned payments on the account | Hold |
|---|---|
| a payment of the account was returned within 60 days before the payment date (60 days or fewer from the latest return to the payment date) | 10 days |
| a returned payment is on record, but none within 60 days | 5 days |
| no returned payment on record | no hold |

**Which payment is held.**
1. Take the account's latest grace-cure payment by check and its latest grace-cure payment by bank transfer (of two of one kind on the same day, the one recorded first).
2. Set aside either one that a returned payment on the account names as the payment it returns, without taking an earlier payment of that kind in its place.
3. Of those not set aside, the later one is the payment examined (of a check and a transfer on the same day, the check).
4. It is held when the days from its receipt to the payment date are fewer than the hold.

**Boundary points.** Latest return 60 days before the payment date: 10-day hold; 61 days: 5-day hold. Under a 10-day hold a check received 9 days before the payment date is held and one received 10 days before is not.

**Hypothetical case.** The latest return was 25 days ago, so the hold is 10 days. The latest grace-cure check, 120.00, was received 6 days ago and has not been returned; the latest grace-cure bank transfer, 80.00, was received 3 days ago but a returned payment names it. The transfer is set aside, the check is examined, 6 is fewer than 10, so 120.00 is added back.
